newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek money rates fall, bonds idle, ecu/drs softer.
newsitem.headline: Greek money rates fall, bonds idle, ecu/drs softer.

text.p: Greek interbank depos and forex forwards were trading lower with the drop more accentuated in short tenors, bonds were little changed in late trade and ecu/drachma was softer on light ecu selling, dealers said.

"Ample liquidity has driven short-term depos and implied drachma rates from forex forwards 30 basis points lower which in turn pulled long tenors lower about a fourth of a point," said a dealer at a foreign bank.

Dealers said liquidity could improve further if sales of T-bills and two-year zeros were short of expiries on Tuesday when a few banks offer retailers more attractive rates on stripped debt instruments.
Greece will issue 12-month T-bills and two-year zeros at a gross rate of 9.60 percent and 9.50 percent respectively.
Bond prices were stable, holding early morning with players showing interest for three-year fixed coupon bonds, dealers said.

"Bonds are holding morning levels," said a dealer at a private bank. "We saw some bids in three-year fixed coupon bonds today but the focus is still on the two-year zeros and 12-month T-bills that go on sale Tuesday."
The mark was quoted at 157.73/83 from Monday's 157.685 fix, the dollar at 274.10/20 drachmas from 275.220 and the ecu at 309.64/74 from 309.330 drachmas.
"There was a constant light selling of ecu/drachma today that pushed it lower to 309.30/35 before rebounding to 309.44/50," said a forex dealer at a private bank. "Trading was quiet."
